findings.title: Restarted flusher gets a new SpansBuffer, losing state of the old one
findings.body: Every restart in _create_process_for_shards builds a new SpansBuffer(shards) and overwrites self.buffers[process_index]. Any in-memory state on the old buffer is dropped. Previously the same buffer was reused across restarts. Also, the old thread (in produce_to_pipe/test mode) is never stopped on restart, so two threads can flush the same shards.

findings.title: Hung threads are not killed on restart; isinstance check uses multiprocessing.Process
findings.body: The kill step checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but processes are created from a spawn context (SpawnProcess), which is not guaranteed to subclass the base multiprocessing.Process class. The kill may be silently skipped, leaving a hung old process running next to its replacement. The same check in join() may skip terminate().

findings.title: join() deadline logic skips terminating remaining processes
findings.body: When the deadline expires, the loop breaks and the remaining processes are never terminated. Also, `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None` treats timeout=0 as no deadline, so join waits forever.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name
findings.body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key "shards", while the other metrics added in this change use "shard". Dashboards will split across two tag keys.

findings.title: Test relies on real sleep after patching time.sleep
findings.body: monkeypatch replaces time.sleep globally with a no-op, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing. The test remains racy because the flusher thread may not have flushed before join. The new limit test only checks the process-to-shard mapping, not restarts or any flush behavior.
